name: sensitive-file-boundary
purpose: Defines where sensitive local files belong, what agents must not read by default, and which metadata may be tracked without exposing secrets.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when a task mentions tokens, keys, credentials, private notes, browser cookies, proprietary documents, user-provided private files, or anything that should not be indexed by AI agents. The real files stay outside git under _private/sensitive/ or in an external secret manager.
how_to_read: Use boundary_model to understand the three layers: tracked policy, ignored local vault, external secret manager.
Use default_deny_paths before running find, rg, workspace-index, monitor collection, source collection, or browser snapshots.
Use allowed_tracked_metadata to record references without storing raw secrets.
Use human_handoff_rules when the agent needs information from a sensitive file.
Run validation_commands after changing sensitive-file policy, maps, snapshots, or collectors.
update_triggers: A new type of sensitive file or secret is introduced.
A tool starts collecting files, snapshots, embeddings, prompts, browser state, or repository maps.
The workspace is prepared for public release or external deployment.
A user asks agents not to see or index a class of files.
Secret storage, environment variable, or external secret-manager rules change.

structure_rules.rule: Track policies, schemas, env var names, secret reference URIs, and redacted metadata; do not track raw secret values or sensitive local documents.
structure_rules.reason: The platform must remain inspectable without exposing credentials or private data.

structure_rules.rule: Agents must not read, list recursively, search, summarize, index, snapshot, embed, or use files under _private/ by default.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked for a central sensitive-file area that AI does not directly inspect.

structure_rules.rule: When sensitive content is needed, the default path is for the human to provide a redacted extract. Explicit one-time permission is required before an agent may inspect a named sensitive file.
structure_rules.reason: Least privilege reduces exposure and avoids copying private data into history, prompts, snapshots, or model context.

structure_rules.rule: Repository maps, monitor snapshots, source collectors, search indexes, generated dashboards, and public artifacts must exclude _private/ and raw secret patterns.
structure_rules.reason: Generated artifacts can leak private data even when git ignores the original files.

structure_rules.rule: Run privacy audit and review monitor snapshots before public release, Vercel deployment, installer packaging, or external sharing.
structure_rules.reason: Private repositories can later become public or be packaged into installable software.

field_guide.meaning: Logical layers for sensitive handling: tracked control plane, ignored local vault, external secret manager.
Paths and patterns agents and collectors must not read or index by default.
Information that can be committed because it does not contain raw sensitive values.
Rules for AI agent interaction with sensitive material.
Process for explicit one-time user authorization when direct inspection is unavoidable.
Commands that prove the boundary remains visible and enforceable.

tracked_examples_only: secret reference placeholders such as op://vault/item/field

allowed_tracked_metadata: external secret-manager reference URI without resolved value
last rotation date when not sensitive
validation command that does not print secret values
prohibited_tracked_content: full private documents unless explicitly approved for repository storage

allowed_without_permission: mention that _private/ exists as a protected local-only boundary
check .gitignore and generated artifacts for exclusion patterns
read this config and tracked policy documents
ask the user for a redacted extract or explicit one-time permission
not_allowed_without_permission: recursive find, rg, cat, sed, open, summarize, embed, screenshot, or snapshot under _private/
copying secrets into prompts, history, evaluations, web searches, generated dashboards, or commits

human_handoff_rules: Ask the user to provide the minimum redacted extract needed for the task.
If exact local file inspection is unavoidable, request explicit one-time permission with path, operation, purpose, and allowed output shape.
Do not store raw extracted content in _history, _research, _docs, snapshots, or final responses.
Record only redacted provenance: source path class, extraction date, field names, and what was intentionally omitted.

tool_exclusion_rules.rule: Do not index local_only_dirs from root-structure-policy into the file index.
Do not traverse _private or outputs; do not include them in document/source snapshots.
Do not collect local sensitive files as research sources.
Do not place raw sensitive values or private file contents into queries.

release_gates: manual review of workspace-monitor/src/generated/workspace-snapshot.json before public deploy
secret scanning or provider push protection when available
confirm no private installer payload before desktop packaging
